title: Quantum Hamming bound for non-degenerate codes
statement:
Let $C \le \mathcal{H}_n$ be a subspace of the $n$-qubit Hilbert space whose complex dimension is $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} C = 2^k$, and suppose $k \le n$. If $C$ is a non-degenerate code correcting $t$ errors — meaning it satisfies the Knill–Laflamme condition $P_C\,E^\dagger F\,P_C = \lambda_{EF}\,P_C$ for all Pauli strings $E,F$ of weight at most $t$, and moreover $P_C\,E^\dagger F\,P_C = 0$ whenever $E \ne F$, where $P_C$ is the orthogonal projection onto $C$ — then
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{t} \binom{n}{j}\, 3^{\,j} \;\le\; 2^{\,n-k}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: C is non-degenerate for t errors (Knill–Laflamme condition on weight-≤t Pauli strings, plus vanishing off-diagonal terms for distinct strings)
